Hi Ana / Miguel —

Great to speak with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our renewal/expansion discussion: 

Call recap:
- Current baseline: ~18M tokens/month across chat + embeddings (prod routes).
- ACME expects 2x growth by Q4 from new triage/chat routing + adding the new summarization model route.
- Primary ask: predictable unit economics and simpler billing for multiple model routes.

Pricing/units we discussed:
- Goal target: $900–1,100 per 1M tokens for blended usage across routes (goal to land around $1,000/1M).
- Proposed step-up tiers (monthly committed): 0–25M: $1,200/1M; 25–75M: $1,000/1M; 75M+: $850/1M (blended billing by tier).
- Token counting: chat tokens + embeddings tokens counted separately but visible in cost breakdowns; we proposed a blended final invoice.

Attachments: I’ve attached the updated pricing deck (redwood-pricing-deck-v3.pdf) and a draft renewal amendment for review.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm target committed volume for the next 12 months (ballpark fine: e.g. 25M / 50M / 100M tokens/mo)?
2) Which of the new routes do you want included in the commitment initially (triage/chat, summarization, batch-embedding)?
3) If the budget target is $1,000/1M (blended), we can prepare a formal amendment and DocuSign — want to get to legal by EOW if possible.

I’ll loop Rishi and Logan on the technical/ops details if you want any extra guarantees (SLA/throughput) included.

Thanks —

Thanks Ana — quick technical+pricing clarification from our side: 

How blended works (short):
- Billing is tiered by aggregated monthly token volume across committed routes.
- Blended $/1M = (sum over tiers of (tier_rate * tokens_in_tier)) / total_tokens — so crossing tiers mid-month gives an invoice that reflects tokens in each tier, not a single higher/lower flat rate.

Model premiums & routing:
- If you add a premium model route (e.g., summarization using a larger variant), we can either: (a) apply a route-specific uplift (+15%) on tokens routed to that model, or (b) create a separate model-bucket that rolls into the same tier math but labeled for visibility.
- For simplicity on the invoice, option (a) keeps one blended number; option (b) gives clearer per-model breakouts but can complicate billing. We usually see customers prefer (a) for renewals.

Throughput & ops notes:
- Adding summarization will increase average latency/compute per request; we recommend enabling dedicated batching for that route and pinning that model to a dedicated pool to preserve SLAs. Logan can share estimated additional GPU capacity.

I’ve added estimates in the HubSpot deal notes: https://hubspot.example/deal/67890 (see 'Ops impact' section).

—Rishi
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
